title: The Sonnet
objective: After this level you can explain how a sonnet's 14 lines are built in its Italian and English forms and where its turn comes.
summary: A sonnet is 14 lines of iambic pentameter. The Italian form turns between octave and sestet; the English form, three quatrains and a couplet, turns before the couplet, as in Sonnet 130.

cards.headline: For twelve lines, this love poem refuses to flatter.
cards.body: "My mistress' eyes are nothing like the sun; / Coral is far more red, than her lips red." Shakespeare's Sonnet 130 compares his beloved, unfavorably, to all the usual beauties of nature. Then the last two lines swerve. That swerve is the secret engine of the sonnet.

cards.headline: Fourteen lines, a little song
cards.body: A sonnet is a 14-line poem, traditionally in iambic pentameter with a set rhyme scheme. The name comes from the Italian sonetto, "a little sound or song." It began among Sicilian court poets in the 13th century, and the Italian poet Petrarch perfected it. In the 16th century, Sir Thomas Wyatt and Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, brought it to England.

mascot.line: Keep this: find the turn, and you've found what the sonnet is really about.

cards.headline: Sonnet 130 turns
cards.body: That shift has a name: the volta, Italian for "turn," the point where a poem's thought changes direction, often flagged by "but" or "yet." Sonnet 130 turns right on cue, before the couplet: "And yet by heaven, I think my love as rare, / As any she belied with false compare." Twelve lines of plain truth were the setup. She's as lovely as any woman praised with false comparisons.

cards.headline: Sonnets: built
learned: A sonnet: 14 lines of iambic pentameter
Italian: octave, sestet, turn after line 8
English: three quatrains and a couplet
The volta is the turn in thought

questions.explanation: A sonnet has 14 lines, traditionally in iambic pentameter.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a sonnet with its description.
questions.explanation: The Italian sonnet's octave has 8 lines rhymed abbaabba and its sestet has 6 lines that answer it. The English sonnet's three quatrains rhyme abab cdcd efef. The volta is Italian for "turn".

questions.prompt: A sonnet's lines are traditionally in iambic pentameter. How many iambs does each line hold?
questions.explanation: Iambic pentameter is five iambs a line, about ten syllables.
